## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Fó shuō shèng-fǎ-yìn jīng* — sub-titled "天竺名阿遮曇摩文圖" ("the Indian name is Ārya-dharma-mudrā [-mudrā?]") — is a single-fascicle Western Jìn 西晉 translation of a discourse on the three "Dharma-seals" (*dharma-mudrā*): all conditioned phenomena are impermanent, all phenomena are without self, and *nirvāṇa* is peace. The Chinese parallels are T99[80] (the *Saṃyukta-āgama* parallel) and [T104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0104) (Shīhù).

**Abstract**

T103 was produced during Dharmarakṣa's Western Jìn career (266–313 CE), recorded in the frontmatter. The Indic source is presumed lost. The discourse is one of the foundational sources for the doctrine of the three Dharma-seals, which would become a fundamental classification of Buddhist doctrine in later East Asian scholasticism.
